literatureReviews.resourceName: Multi-user conflict resolution mechanisms for smart home environments
literatureReviews.resourceInsights: The study highlights that while smart homes are often designed for a single user, conflicts arise when multiple people have contradictory preferences for lighting, temperature, or music in the same space. A key takeaway is the importance of "Special Cases" (e.g., illness, exams, or guests). The system should automatically prioritize users in these states. The research defines three approaches: Automatic (system decides), Mediated (system asks users to discuss), and Hybrid.
literatureReviews.comments: This paper directly supports the "Co-op" and "Conflict Resolution" features of our project. It provides a theoretical framework for why a client needs a simple way to manage guest access while more advanced users need a priority system for their automations.

literatureReviews.resourceName: My experience with Apple’s HomeKit for over two years
literatureReviews.resourceInsights:
Even high-end ecosystems suffer from "No Response" errors due to poor Wi-Fi or Bluetooth connectivity between devices and the central hub.
Users find it difficult to set up truly useful automations (like motion-activated lighting) that don't become annoying over time due to technical limitations.
There is a lack of high-quality, diverse hardware (especially light switches) that fits seamlessly into a professional smart home setup.
literatureReviews.comments: This justifies the "Hardware Specialist" persona and his focus on local storage and Zigbee/Matter protocols to avoid the "No Response" cloud-dependency issues mentioned in the article.

literatureReviews.resourceName: How will AR and MR impact the smart home experience?
literatureReviews.resourceInsights: he article highlights that AR allows users to "see" digital information in physical space, moving away from 2D lists on a phone screen to 3D interaction.It discusses the ability to look at a device and have its specific controls appear instantly, reducing the "search time" in traditional apps. AR can visualize invisible data like Wi-Fi signals, heat distribution, or energy flow, which are otherwise impossible to perceive.
literatureReviews.comments: It validates our Observational Research finding regarding "Hidden Maintenance"—using AR to see through walls or into machines to identify faults.

literatureReviews.resourceName: Best smart home systems: Top ecosystems for every house
literatureReviews.resourceInsights:
The article discusses the necessity of a central "brain" or hub to ensure devices from different manufacturers can communicate.
It highlights how choosing a system (like Alexa vs. HomeKit) often limits which hardware you can buy, creating a "walled garden" effect.
There is a constant trade-off between "plug-and-play" simplicity for casual users and the deep customization desired by enthusiasts.
literatureReviews.comments: This justifies the "Agnostic Core" of INTELLIDEN. It also validates our multi-platform UI approach

observationalResearch.target: User entering the home with hands full.
observationalResearch.behavior: The user (Andrei) approached the door carrying several bags. He attempted to reach for his phone in his pocket to unlock the smart lock but nearly dropped a bag. He eventually gave up on the phone and waited for a roommate to open the door from the inside.
observationalResearch.comments: Demonstrates a clear need for "zero-touch" or gesture-based unlocking via the Smartwatch

observationalResearch.behavior: The user (Marcus) noticed the dishwasher was making a strange noise. He spent 10 minutes looking for the physical manual and another 5 minutes trying to find the specific error code on his tablet.
observationalResearch.comments: Justifies the AR Glasses feature: a spatial overlay that shows real-time diagnostics and "X-ray" views of internal components directly over the machine

observationalResearch.target: Two roommates in the living room.
observationalResearch.behavior: Ioana set the temperature to 22°C for her workout. Ten minutes later, Maria entered, felt too hot, and manually changed it to 19°C. Neither realized the other had a specific reason for their setting, leading to a verbal disagreement.
observationalResearch.comments: The system needs to show "Active Intent"  to all users.
